<h3>Eligibility</h3>
<div class="faqs">
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>What are the eligibility requirements?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>In short, all applicants must be the <strong><u>child</u></strong> of a Marine or a Navy Corpsman, Chaplain or Religious Programs specialist attached to a Marine unit, have a cumulative GPA of 2.00, and have an adjusted gross income at or below the financial eligibility threshold determined by the Foundation on an annual basis. For the 2027-2028 application, the threshold is $134,000 for tax year 2025.</p>
<p>Additional documents may be required during the application process to verify eligibility. Applicants must also submit a completed application with all required documents by the application deadline.</p>
<p>For more information about eligibility requirements, visit <a href="http://www.mcsf.org/eligibility">www.mcsf.org/eligibility.</a></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>Do all eligible applicants receive an award?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Yes! That said, applicants must meet ALL <a href="http://www.mcsf.org/eligibility" target="_blank" rel="noopener">eligibility requirements</a> AND submit a completed application with all required and requested documents by the deadline. If applicants submit their application with missing or incorrect documents, they will be considered ineligible for an award. Ineligible applicants may reapply in future years.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>My family's income is higher than your limit. Should I still apply?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>You can apply if your family’s income is over the threshold ($134,000 for tax year 2025), but there is no guarantee you’ll be awarded a scholarship. You will need to provide a thorough explanation of your family’s financial need, and you may be required to provide additional documents to substantiate your explanation. <strong>Only applicants with extreme extenuating financial circumstances will be considered.</strong> Note, extenuating circumstances <strong>do NOT</strong> include: “I am paying for college on my own” or “I am attending an expensive college.”</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>Are stepchildren of Marines/Sailors eligible to apply?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Yes! Stepchildren may be required to provide additional documentation to show proof of their relationship to the qualifying military parent (typically a tax document and/or a marriage certificate). The military stepparent must remain married to the biological parent for continued eligibility.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>I'm a part-time student. Am I still eligible to receive a scholarship?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Yes! Part-time students are eligible to receive a scholarship.</p>
</div>
</div>

<p>No. If you’ve already earned an undergraduate degree or completed all your undergraduate courses, then you’re not eligible for a scholarship. <div id="application" class="faq_section">
<h3>Application</h3>
<div class="faqs">
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>How do I apply?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Our online application is open from January 1 through March 1 each year. Learn more at <a href="http://www.mcsf.org/apply" target="_blank" rel="noopener">www.mcsf.org/apply</a>. We do not provide or accept paper applications, and all required documents must be submitted electronically.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>When does the application open and what is the award timeline?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<h3><strong>UNDERGRADUATE/ASSOCIATE SCHOLARSHIP TIMELINE</strong></h3>
<p><strong>January 1 </strong>– Application opens</p>
<p><strong>March 1 </strong>– Application deadline</p>
<p><strong>May 31</strong> – Award decisions e-mailed to students</p>
<p><strong>August 1 </strong>– First batch of scholarship payments sent to schools (subsequent batches sent approximately twice a month)</p>
<p><strong>November 1 </strong>– Award Acceptance deadline</p>
<p><strong>December/January </strong>– Transfer paperwork due (if applicable)</p>
<p> </p>
<h3><strong>CAREER & TECHNICAL EDUCATION SCHOLARSHIP TIMELINE</strong></h3>
<p>Application available all year.</p>
<p>Applications processed monthly.</p>

<div id="tax_documents" class="faq_section">
<h3>Tax Documents</h3>
<div class="faqs">
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>What tax forms are accepted?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>All pages of the <strong>2025 federal tax return (IRS-1040)</strong> <strong>on which you are claimed.</strong></p>
<p><strong>Even if you file your own taxes, you may also have to provide your parents’ taxes.</strong> Check out the next question to determine which document we’ll need.</p>
<p>You’re <strong>not</strong> required to provide the taxes for your qualifying military parent unless that’s the parent that claims you; see “Other Documents Needed” on our <a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a> if your military parent doesn’t claim you.</p>
<p><strong>Acceptable federal tax forms are:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Federal (US) 1040 – all two pages*</li>
<li>Federal (US) 1040-SR – all three pages*</li>
</ul>
<p>*You’ll need to submit all pages of IRS form 1040, <span class="TrackChangeTextInsertion TrackedChange SCXW135604940 BCX8"><span class="TextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8" lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8">which is two or three pages based on the version (you </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8">are not required to</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8"> provide the supplemental pages that often </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8">accompany</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8"> the 1040 form</span></span></span><span class="TrackChangeTextInsertion TrackedChange SCXW135604940 BCX8"><span class="TextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8" lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8"> unless you are listed on a statement of dependents</span></span></span><span class="TrackChangeTextInsertion TrackedChange SCXW135604940 BCX8"><span class="TextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8" lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW135604940 BCX8">)</span></span></span>. The tax document must have your full name listed as a dependent, and the tax filer’s Adjusted Gross Income (AGI).</p>
<p><strong>Unacceptable tax forms include:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Form 1040-ES</li>
<li>Form 1040-X</li>
<li>Tax transcripts</li>
<li>Tax Compliance Reports</li>
<li>Summary pages</li>
</ul>
<p>The general IRS site for all forms is: <a href="http://www.irs.gov">http://www.irs.gov</a></p>
<p>For more information regarding tax requirements, visit our <strong><a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a>.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>How do I know if I should submit my parents' tax return or my own tax return?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Determine the type of student you are by visiting the <a href="https://studentaid.gov/apply-for-aid/fafsa/filling-out/dependency" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Department of Education’s Federal Student Aid website</a>.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Dependent applicants:</strong>
<ul>
<li>Must provide the parent’s taxes on which they’re claimed (this means the dependent’s will appear in the Dependents box – or on the supplemental List of Dependents form).</li>
<li><strong>Even if you file your own taxes, you must provide your parents’ taxes.</strong></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>If you’re a dependent student and aren’t claimed on your parents’ taxes, then you’ll need to provide your parents’ taxes AND your own taxes.</strong></li>
<li><strong>Independent applicants</strong> must provide their own taxes.</li>
</ul>
<p><span class="TrackChangeTextInsertion TrackedChange SCXW200911248 BCX8"><span class="TextRun SCXW200911248 BCX8" lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW200911248 BCX8">Not living with your parents, </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW200911248 BCX8">being responsible for</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW200911248 BCX8"> your own educational expenses, or not being claimed by your parents on your tax forms </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW200911248 BCX8">doesn’t</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW200911248 BCX8"> change our requirements.</span></span></span><span class="EOP SCXW200911248 BCX8" data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p>
<p>For more information regarding tax requirements, visit our <strong><a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a>.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>I’m considered a dependent student, but I'm paying for my own education. Do I still have to submit my parents' tax return?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Yes. Dependent students must submit their parents’ taxes regardless of whether their parents are paying for their education. Your name should appear on the tax 1040 form in the Dependents box or on the supplemental List of Dependents form.</p>
<p>If you’re a dependent student and aren’t claimed on your parents’ taxes, you’ll need to provide your parents’ taxes AND your own taxes.</p>
<p>Not living with your parents, being responsible for your own educational expenses, or not being claimed by your parents on your tax forms doesn’t change our requirements.</p>
<p>For more information regarding tax requirements, visit our <a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><strong>Required Application Documents page.</strong></a></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>My parents are divorced or separated. Whose tax document should I use?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Submit the taxes for the parent who claims you (your name will appear on the 1040 tax form in the Dependents box or on the supplemental List of Dependents form). You’re not required to provide the taxes for your qualifying military parent unless that’s the parent that claims you.</p>
<p>For more information regarding tax requirements, visit our <strong><a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a>.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>What if I, or my parents, don’t file a tax return?</p>

</div>

<p>Provide an IRS Verification of Non-Filing Letter for 2025. If you haven’t requested from the IRS, you can provide a <strong>Statement of Non-filing of a Federal Tax Return</strong> form in lieu of taxes. The form can be found within the application and must be signed by you and your parents. However, the IRS Verification letter must be provided before a final award decision can be made. <span class="NormalTextRun TrackChangeHoverSelectHighlightRed SCXW135284612 BCX8">Applicants who </span><span class="NormalTextRun TrackChangeHoverSelectHighlightRed SCXW135284612 BCX8">fail to</span><span class="NormalTextRun TrackChangeHoverSelectHighlightRed SCXW135284612 BCX8"> provide the official confirmation risk being </span><span class="NormalTextRun TrackChangeHoverSelectHighlightRed SCXW135284612 BCX8">determined</span><span class="NormalTextRun TrackChangeHoverSelectHighlightRed SCXW135284612 BCX8"> ineligible for a scholarship award.</span></p>

<div id="military_documents" class="faq_section">

<p>Military parent is currently on active duty OR is a drilling reservist:  <strong>Statement of Service</strong> (dated after December 1, 2026).</p>

</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>What is a DD214 (Member-4 version) form?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>This document was provided to your military parent upon discharge from the military and should be used if your parent is no longer serving in the Marine Corps or Navy.</p>
<p>The <strong>Character of Service</strong> on the DD214 must read: <strong>HONORABLE</strong>. Read the next question to find where this is located on the DD214.</p>
<p>The following <strong>CANNOT</strong> be accepted in place of a DD214 Member-4: Honorable Discharge Certificate, DD214 Member-1 forms (or short forms), DD214s that don’t indicate “Character of Service,” letters from Veterans’ Affairs, disability documents, duty orders, or military IDs.</p>
<p>For more information regarding military parent document requirements, visit our <strong><a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a>.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>Where can I find the “Character of Service” on the DD214 (Member-4 version)?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>

<p>Some DD214s don’t show the character of service. That means the document is not the final version and your military parent will need to obtain a final version at: <a href="http://www.archives.gov/veterans">www.archives.gov/veterans</a>.</p>

<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>What if I don’t have my parent’s DD214 (Member-4 version), or proof of their honorable service?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>The DD214 (Member-4) form is a required document for our application. The Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation is a non-profit and is not associated with the National Archives or the Marine Corps and unfortunately, we do not have the capability to coordinate with them to obtain military records.</p>
<p>If you cannot get a copy of your parent’s DD214 (Member-4 version), we invite you to apply for our scholarship in future years once you have obtained a copy.</p>
<p>For more information regarding military parent document requirements, visit our <strong><a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a>.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>My parent is currently on active duty or is a drilling reservist. What kind of service proof do you require?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>If your parent is still on Active Duty or is a drilling Reservist you’ll need to submit their <strong>Statement of Service</strong>.  The Statement of Service must be on official US Department of Defense (Marine Corps or Navy) letterhead and signed by the Adjutant, Personnel Officer, Executive Officer, or Commanding Officer of your parent’s current unit and <strong>dated after December 1, 2026</strong>.</p>
<p>The following documents <strong>CANNOT</strong> be accepted in lieu of the Statement of Service: duty orders, military IDs, Honorable Discharge Certificate, DD214 forms, letters from Veterans Affairs, or disability documents.</p>
<p>For more information regarding military parent document requirements, visit our <strong><a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a>.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>My parent served primarily as a drilling reservist. What kind of military documentation do you require?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>We need your parent’s final DD214 as listed in the question above. If your parent doesn’t have a DD214 documenting the full length of their service, then we require the most recent DD214 with character of service AND one of the following documents:</p>
<ul>
<li>Career Retirement Credit Report (CRCR)</li>
<li>Transfer to the Individual Ready Reserve (IRR) Letter on DOD letterhead</li>
<li>Official Marine Corps or Navy Retirement Letter</li>
</ul>
<p>For more information regarding military parent document requirements, visit our <strong><a href="https://mcsf.scholarshipapps.org/required_docs.cfm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Required Application Documents page</a>.</strong></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>My parent was killed in action, killed in service, or killed in training. What service document do you require?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>You’ll need to provide the Report of Casualty DD 1300 Form. <span class="TrackChangeTextInsertion TrackedChange SCXW180908993 BCX8"><span class="TextRun SCXW180908993 BCX8" lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW180908993 BCX8">Have more questions about this?</span></span></span><span class="TrackChangeTextInsertion TrackedChange SCXW180908993 BCX8"><span class="TextRun SCXW180908993 BCX8" lang="EN-US" xml:lang="EN-US" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW180908993 BCX8"> Contact us!</span></span></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>My parent is wounded, ill, or injured. What service document do you require?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Depending on your military parent’s service status (discharged, active duty, or drilling reservist) you’ll need to provide the appropriate service document as indicated above.</p>
<p>If your parent has been placed on the Marine Corps <strong>Permanent Disability Retired List (PDRL)</strong>, then you’ll need to also provide documentation from the Marine Corps assigning your parent to PDRL.</p>
<p>We cannot accept documents from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as PDRL is different from a VA disability rating.</p>
<p>Have more questions about this? Contact us!</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="photograph" class="faq_section">
<h3>Photograph</h3>
<div class="faqs">
<div class="faq">
<div class="question">
<p>What are the requirements for the photograph I need to include in my application?</p>
<span class="arrow">
<i class="fas fa-chevron-right"></i>
</span>
</div>
<div class="answer">
<p>Provide a photo that is at least 500KB and the highest resolution possible (300 dpi preferred). Professional photos (senior portraits or otherwise) are preferred. Examples can be viewed at <a href="https://www.mcsf.org/photo-guidelines/">www.mcsf.org/photo-guidelines</a>.</p>
<p><strong>All photos <u>must</u> meet the following requirements:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>High resolution (300 dpi preferred)</li>
<li>In color</li>
<li>Clear view of your face (no sunglasses, hats, etc)</li>
<li>Suitable for Scholarship Foundation publications to include: our website, newsletters, donor communications, and/or event materials</li>
<li>Taken in an appropriate setting and represents you in a positive way</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Do NOT submit:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Selfies</li>
<li>Cropped photos</li>
<li>Photos with other people in them</li>
<li>Photos with distracting elements in the background</li>
<li>Photos that don’t clearly show your face (such as hands near face, wearing hat/sunglasses, etc.)</li>
<li>Photos that are inappropriate or provocative</li>
<li>Poor quality, grainy, scanned or highly pixelated photos</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
</div>
